title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
description: A beginner-friendly guide to Python that teaches practical automation of everyday computer tasks such as renaming files, scraping websites, filling spreadsheets and sending emails, with no prior programming experience needed.

title: Learning Python
description: A comprehensive and detailed reference to the Python language covering types, functions, classes, modules and exceptions, suited to learners who want a thorough understanding of how Python works.

title: Fluent Python
description: Explains the advanced features of Python such as data models, decorators, generators, concurrency and metaprogramming, helping experienced programmers write clear, idiomatic and efficient Python code.

title: Python for Data Analysis
description: Introduces data wrangling in Python using pandas and NumPy, covering cleaning, reshaping, aggregation and time series so analysts can turn raw data into useful results.

title: Head First Python
description: A visual, puzzle-driven introduction to Python for beginners, covering lists, functions, web apps and databases through hands-on exercises rather than dense theory.

title: Think Python
description: A gentle introduction to programming with Python that builds computational thinking step by step, from variables and loops to recursion and object-oriented design, ideal for first-year students.

title: Effective Python
description: Offers 90 specific ways to write better Python, covering Pythonic style, data structures, concurrency and testing, for developers who already know the basics.

title: Eloquent JavaScript
description: A modern introduction to JavaScript that teaches programming concepts, the browser and Node.js through clear explanations and projects, suitable for newcomers to web programming.

title: JavaScript: The Good Parts
description: A short, opinionated book that highlights the reliable core of JavaScript and warns about its confusing features, aimed at developers who want cleaner and safer code.

title: You Do Not Know JS Yet
description: A deep exploration of how JavaScript really works, covering scope, closures, objects and types, for programmers who want to master the language beyond surface syntax.

title: The C Programming Language
authors: Brian W. Kernighan; Dennis M. Ritchie
description: The classic concise guide to C written by its creators, covering the language, pointers, memory and the standard library, and a foundation for systems programming.

title: Effective Java
description: A collection of best practices for Java covering object creation, generics, lambdas, streams and concurrency, written for developers who want robust and maintainable Java software.

title: Head First Java
description: A brain-friendly introduction to Java and object-oriented programming using visuals, puzzles and short exercises, designed for students writing their first Java programs.

title: Core Java Volume I Fundamentals
description: A thorough reference to the Java language and core libraries, including collections, generics, exceptions and concurrency, used as a main textbook for university Java courses.

title: A Tour of C++
description: A compact overview of modern C++ by its creator, covering classes, templates, the standard library and concurrency for programmers who already know another language.

title: Clean Code
description: Teaches how to write readable, maintainable software through naming, functions, formatting, error handling and refactoring, with many real code examples to improve quality.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
description: Practical advice on the craft of software development, including debugging, automation, design and career habits, presented as short tips useful to programmers at any level.

title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
authors: Erich Gamma; Richard Helm; Ralph Johnson; John Vlissides
description: Catalogs 23 classic object-oriented design patterns such as Singleton, Observer and Factory, explaining when and how to apply each in software architecture.

title: Refactoring
description: Shows how to improve the structure of existing code safely through small, well-defined steps, with a catalog of refactorings and guidance on detecting code smells.

title: Code Complete
description: A practical handbook of software construction covering design, coding, debugging, testing and teamwork, based on research and experience, for developers building quality software.

title: The Mythical Man-Month
description: Classic essays on managing large software projects, including why adding people to a late project makes it later, and lessons on planning, teams and system design.

title: Software Engineering
description: A university textbook covering the software lifecycle, requirements, architecture, agile methods, testing and project management for students of software engineering.

title: Introduction to Algorithms
authors: Thomas H. Cormen; Charles E. Leiserson; Ronald L. Rivest; Clifford Stein
description: The standard rigorous algorithms textbook covering sorting, graphs, dynamic programming and complexity analysis with proofs, used in advanced undergraduate and graduate courses.

title: Algorithms
description: Presents essential algorithms and data structures such as sorting, searching, graphs and strings with Java implementations and visual explanations, widely used in university courses.

title: The Algorithm Design Manual
description: Teaches how to design and choose algorithms for real problems, with a catalog of common problem types and war stories, useful for interviews and coursework.

title: Grokking Algorithms
description: An illustrated beginner-friendly introduction to algorithms and data structures, explaining searching, sorting, graphs and dynamic programming through simple pictures and examples.

title: Algorithm Design
description: Explains algorithm design techniques such as greedy methods, divide and conquer, dynamic programming and network flow through problem-driven examples, for advanced students.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms in Java
authors: Michael T. Goodrich; Roberto Tamassia; Michael H. Goldwasser
description: Covers arrays, linked lists, trees, hash tables and graphs with Java implementations and analysis, a standard text for a second computer science course.

title: Cracking the Coding Interview
description: Contains 189 programming interview questions with solutions on data structures and algorithms, plus advice on preparing for technical interviews at software companies.

title: Programming Pearls
description: Short essays on solving real programming problems with clever algorithms and data structures, emphasizing problem definition, performance and elegant design.

title: The Art of Computer Programming Volume 1
description: A deeply mathematical treatment of fundamental algorithms and information structures, considered a landmark work in computer science for advanced readers.

title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras and TensorFlow
description: A practical guide to building machine learning and deep learning models in Python, from linear models and trees to neural networks, with code and projects.

title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
description: A rigorous textbook on probabilistic machine learning covering Bayesian methods, graphical models, kernels and neural networks, intended for advanced students with strong mathematics.

title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
authors: Trevor Hastie; Robert Tibshirani; Jerome Friedman
description: A mathematically detailed reference on statistical learning covering regression, classification, boosting, support vector machines and unsupervised methods for data mining.

title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
authors: Gareth James; Daniela Witten; Trevor Hastie; Robert Tibshirani
description: An accessible introduction to statistical learning and machine learning methods with practical examples, suited to beginners who want to analyze data without heavy mathematics.

title: Deep Learning
authors: Ian Goodfellow; Yoshua Bengio; Aaron Courville
description: A comprehensive textbook on deep neural networks covering optimization, convolutional and recurrent networks and generative models, with the mathematical background needed.

title: Machine Learning: A Probabilistic Perspective
description: A broad and detailed textbook presenting machine learning through probability and statistics, covering classical models, Bayesian inference and graphical models.

title: Python Machine Learning
description: A hands-on guide to machine learning with Python, scikit-learn and TensorFlow, covering classification, clustering, neural networks and model evaluation with code.

title: Deep Learning with Python
description: Written by the creator of Keras, this book teaches deep learning for computer vision and text with practical Python code and intuitive explanations.

title: Machine Learning Yearning
description: A short practical guide on how to structure machine learning projects, including setting up data splits, error analysis and deciding what to improve next.

title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
description: A free online book explaining neural networks and backpropagation step by step with interactive examples, a gentle starting point for beginners in deep learning.

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
authors: Richard S. Sutton; Andrew G. Barto
description: The standard textbook on reinforcement learning covering Markov decision processes, temporal difference learning and policy methods for students and researchers.

title: Machine Learning
description: An early and clear textbook covering core machine learning ideas such as decision trees, neural networks, Bayesian learning and concept learning, suited to university courses.

title: The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book
description: A concise overview of machine learning concepts and algorithms in about one hundred pages, useful for beginners who want the essentials quickly.

title: Speech and Language Processing
description: A comprehensive textbook on natural language processing and speech covering parsing, semantics, machine translation and neural language models for advanced students.

title: Natural Language Processing with Python
authors: Steven Bird; Ewan Klein; Edward Loper
description: Introduces text processing with Python and the NLTK library, covering tokenization, tagging, classification and parsing through practical exercises for beginners.

title: Natural Language Processing with Transformers
authors: Lewis Tunstall; Leandro von Werra; Thomas Wolf
description: A practical guide to building language applications with Hugging Face transformers, covering text classification, question answering, summarization and fine-tuning.

title: Designing Machine Learning Systems
description: Explains how to build reliable production machine learning systems, covering data pipelines, deployment, monitoring and iteration for engineers working with real applications.

title: Prompt Engineering for Generative AI
description: Teaches techniques for writing effective prompts for large language models and image generators, with patterns for reliable and repeatable generative AI applications.

title: Build a Large Language Model From Scratch
description: Walks through building a GPT-style large language model in Python step by step, covering tokenization, attention, pretraining and fine-tuning for advanced learners.

title: Generative Deep Learning
description: Explains how generative models such as GANs, autoencoders and diffusion models work, with Python code for creating images, text and music.

title: Life 3.0
description: A non-technical exploration of how artificial intelligence may shape society, jobs, ethics and the future of humanity, aimed at general readers curious about AI.

title: Human Compatible
description: Argues that artificial intelligence must be designed to remain under human control and aligned with human values, discussing risks and a new approach to AI safety.

title: Superintelligence
description: Examines possible paths to machine superintelligence, the risks it poses and strategies for control, a thoughtful discussion of the long-term future of artificial intelligence.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Guide for Thinking Humans
description: A clear and balanced look at what current artificial intelligence can and cannot do, explaining machine learning and its limits for non-specialists.

title: Data Science from Scratch
description: Teaches data science fundamentals by building tools such as linear regression, clustering and neural networks from scratch in Python, ideal for beginners.

title: Python Data Science Handbook
description: A reference to the Python data science stack including NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and scikit-learn, with practical examples for analysis and machine learning.

title: Storytelling with Data
description: Teaches how to present data clearly through effective charts, design choices and narrative, aimed at analysts who need to communicate findings to others.

title: R for Data Science
description: Introduces the data science workflow in R covering importing, tidying, transforming, visualizing and modeling data using the tidyverse, suitable for beginners.

title: Practical Statistics for Data Scientists
description: Covers the statistical concepts most relevant to data science, such as sampling, regression and classification, with Python and R examples for practitioners.

title: Think Stats
description: Introduces probability and statistics using Python programming and real datasets, helping students who can code learn to analyze data and test hypotheses.

title: Bayesian Methods for Hackers
description: A programming-first introduction to Bayesian inference using Python and PyMC, explaining probabilistic modeling through code and practical data examples.

title: Doing Data Science
description: Gives a realistic view of working as a data scientist, covering algorithms, modeling, data engineering and ethics through contributions from practicing experts.

title: Naked Statistics
description: An entertaining non-technical introduction to statistical ideas such as correlation, probability and inference, showing how data is used and misused in everyday life.

title: Mining of Massive Datasets
authors: Jure Leskovec; Anand Rajaraman; Jeffrey D. Ullman
description: Covers algorithms for mining very large datasets including MapReduce, similarity search, recommendation systems and link analysis for advanced students.

title: Database System Concepts
authors: Abraham Silberschatz; Henry F. Korth; S. Sudarshan
description: A major university textbook on database systems covering the relational model, SQL, normalization, transactions and storage, used in core database courses.

title: Fundamentals of Database Systems
description: Explains database design, the relational model, SQL, indexing and transaction processing with many examples, a common textbook for undergraduate database courses.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
description: Explores the principles behind modern data systems including replication, partitioning, transactions, streams and distributed consistency, for engineers building scalable applications.

title: Learning SQL
description: A beginner-friendly guide to SQL covering queries, joins, grouping, subqueries and data modification with clear examples for working with relational databases.

title: MongoDB: The Definitive Guide
authors: Shannon Bradshaw; Eoin Brazil; Kristina Chodorow
description: Covers the MongoDB document database including data modeling, queries, indexing, aggregation and replication, useful for developers building NoSQL applications.

title: Hadoop: The Definitive Guide
description: Explains Hadoop, HDFS and MapReduce for storing and processing large datasets across clusters, with practical guidance for big data engineers.

title: Spark: The Definitive Guide
description: A practical guide to Apache Spark covering structured APIs, streaming and machine learning for processing big data at scale.

title: Operating System Concepts
authors: Abraham Silberschatz; Peter B. Galvin; Greg Gagne
description: The widely used operating systems textbook covering processes, threads, scheduling, memory management, file systems and protection for undergraduate computer science students.

title: Modern Operating Systems
description: A readable textbook on operating system principles including processes, memory, file systems and security, with case studies of real systems such as Linux and Windows.

title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
authors: Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau; Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau
description: A friendly introduction to operating systems organized around virtualization, concurrency and persistence, free online and well suited to first-time learners.

title: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
authors: James F. Kurose; Keith W. Ross
description: Introduces computer networks starting from applications and moving down to the physical layer, covering HTTP, TCP, IP and wireless networks for beginners.

title: Computer Networks
authors: Andrew S. Tanenbaum; David J. Wetherall
description: A thorough textbook on network layers, protocols and architectures, from physical transmission to applications, widely used in networking courses.

title: TCP/IP Illustrated Volume 1
description: A detailed look at the TCP/IP protocol suite using packet traces to show exactly how protocols behave, intended for readers who want deep networking knowledge.

title: Cryptography and Network Security
description: Covers encryption, authentication, key management and network security protocols, giving students a broad foundation in cybersecurity principles and practice.

title: Security Engineering
description: Explains how to build dependable systems that withstand attack, covering cryptography, access control, human factors and real-world case studies in computer security.

title: The Web Application Hackers Handbook
description: A detailed guide to finding and exploiting vulnerabilities in web applications, covering injection, authentication and session flaws for security testers.

title: Learning React
description: A beginner-friendly introduction to building user interfaces with React, covering components, hooks, state management and data fetching in modern JavaScript.

title: Node.js Design Patterns
description: Teaches design patterns and asynchronous programming in Node.js for building scalable server software, including streams, modules and microservices.

title: Docker Deep Dive
description: Explains containers and Docker from the basics to images, networking, volumes and orchestration, helping beginners package and run applications reliably.

title: The Phoenix Project
authors: Gene Kim; Kevin Behr; George Spafford
description: A novel about an IT team rescuing a failing project that teaches DevOps principles such as flow, feedback and continuous improvement in an engaging story.

title: Site Reliability Engineering
authors: Betsy Beyer; Chris Jones; Jennifer Petoff; Niall Richard Murphy
description: Describes how Google runs production systems, covering monitoring, incident response, automation and reliability practices for engineers operating large services.

title: Kubernetes: Up and Running
authors: Brendan Burns; Joe Beda; Kelsey Hightower
description: A practical introduction to deploying and managing containerized applications with Kubernetes, covering pods, services, scaling and configuration in the cloud.

title: Introduction to the Theory of Computation
description: A clear introduction to automata, formal languages, computability and complexity theory, including NP-completeness, written for advanced computer science students.

title: Computer Organization and Design
authors: David A. Patterson; John L. Hennessy
description: Explains how computer hardware and software interact, covering instruction sets, processors, pipelining and memory hierarchy, for students of computer architecture.

title: Concrete Mathematics
authors: Ronald L. Graham; Donald E. Knuth; Oren Patashnik
description: A foundation in the mathematics used to analyze algorithms, including sums, recurrences, number theory and generating functions, for advanced computer science students.

title: Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
description: A standard textbook covering logic, sets, proofs, graphs and combinatorics with many computer science applications, used in introductory discrete mathematics courses.

title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
description: A classic text that teaches programming concepts such as abstraction, recursion and interpreters using Scheme, aimed at serious learners of computer science.

title: Attention Is All You Need
authors: Ashish Vaswani; Noam Shazeer; Niki Parmar; Jakob Uszkoreit; Llion Jones; Aidan N. Gomez; Lukasz Kaiser; Illia Polosukhin
description: Introduces the Transformer architecture, which relies on self-attention instead of recurrence and became the basis of modern large language models and machine translation systems.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
authors: Jacob Devlin; Ming-Wei Chang; Kenton Lee; Kristina Toutanova
description: Presents BERT, a bidirectional transformer pretrained on large text corpora and fine-tuned for many language tasks, setting new results in natural language understanding.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
authors: Tom B. Brown; Benjamin Mann; Nick Ryder; Melanie Subbiah; et al.
description: Describes GPT-3, a very large language model that performs many tasks from just a few examples in the prompt without fine-tuning, a key step for generative AI.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis; Ethan Perez; Aleksandra Piktus; Fabio Petroni; et al.
description: Proposes retrieval-augmented generation, which combines a language model with a document retriever so answers are grounded in external knowledge, improving factual question answering.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
authors: Kaiming He; Xiangyu Zhang; Shaoqing Ren; Jian Sun
description: Introduces residual networks with skip connections that make very deep neural networks easier to train, achieving breakthrough results in image recognition.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
description: Presents the Adam optimizer, an efficient method for training neural networks that adapts learning rates using estimates of gradient moments, now widely used in deep learning.

title: Generative Adversarial Nets
authors: Ian Goodfellow; Jean Pouget-Abadie; Mehdi Mirza; Bing Xu; et al.
description: Introduces generative adversarial networks, where a generator and a discriminator compete, allowing neural networks to produce realistic synthetic data such as images.

title: MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters
description: Describes the MapReduce programming model and its implementation at Google for processing very large datasets in parallel across clusters of commodity machines.
